transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I... I guess I'm here because things have just gotten to a point where I couldn't keep it to myself anymore. I'm a manager over at the distribution center, have been for years, and usually I can just push through whatever's going on, you know? Just keep the floor moving, keep the guys on task. But lately, it's like this heavy fog just rolled in and parked itself right over me. And it's not just the fog, it's... well, I started having these thoughts. Really dark thoughts. I'd be driving home from a 12-hour shift, exhausted, and I'd catch myself thinking, "What if I just closed my eyes?" Or I'd be sitting in my chair at home, looking at my wife, and my brain would just whisper that maybe her life, maybe the kids' lives, would just be so much easier, so much better, if I just... didn't wake up the next morning. It started happening so often, and it got so loud in my head, that it really started to scare me. I've never been one to complain, never even finished high school, just worked hard my whole life, but this... this was different. It scared me enough that I actually broke down and told my supervisor about it. He's a good guy, known him a long time, and he's the one who told me I needed to come see someone. So, here I am.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, like hobbies or spending time with your family?

Yeah, I have. It's... it's actually funny you ask that, because my wife was just saying something about it the other day, and she's usually pretty quiet about that kind of stuff. But I used to always be doing something, you know? Keeping busy. Like, I've got this little patch out in the backyard where I grow tomatoes. Better Boy tomatoes, mostly, because they hold up real good in the summer heat. I used to be out there every single evening after work, checking the soil, pruning them back, tying the vines up to the stakes. It was my quiet time. And if I wasn't out in the dirt, I'd be out in the garage. I have this old workbench out there, and I'd just stand there for hours sanding wood. I didn't even have to be building anything in particular, I'd just take a piece of scrap pine or oak and work it until it was perfectly smooth. Just feeling the grain under my hands... it settled my mind after dealing with the chaos at the distribution center all day. 

And it was the same way with people, too. I've been a Falcons fan my whole life, through all the miserable seasons, and I used to never miss a game on TV. I'd be right there in my chair, yelling at the screen. And on Sunday mornings at church, I was always the guy who'd stay an extra hour after the service ended, just standing out in the parking lot talking to folks, catching up on everyone's week, shooting the breeze. 

But lately... man, I don't know. Lately I just look at all that like it belongs to somebody else. I walk past the garden and the weeds are choking out the plants, and I just stare at it and keep walking. I look at my workbench, and it just seems like a pile of junk. I see the game is on, and I don't even care what the score is. And at church, as soon as the preacher says 'amen,' I'm making a beeline straight for my truck so I don't have to talk to a single soul. It's like the guy who used to enjoy all those things just packed up and left, and I'm just... I'm just sitting here in his house, not knowing what to do with his stuff. The joy is just completely drained right out of it all.
Have there ever been times when you felt unusually high, extremely energetic, or so good that you didn't feel like you needed much sleep?

Well, it's funny you ask that, because... well, yeah. Actually, right before this whole heavy fog rolled in and I started having those dark thoughts, I went through this... this spell. It wasn't like how I feel now, not at all. It was like I had a motor running inside me that just wouldn't quit. 

I remember it started around the time we were getting ready for the big holiday push at the distribution center. Usually, that time of year stresses me out, but this time, man, I felt like I could take on the whole world. I was coming in early, staying late, and I swear I was running on maybe three, four hours of sleep a night. I'd wake up at 3:00 AM, eyes wide open, and my brain would just be going a mile a minute. I'd be laying in bed thinking about how we could reorganize the loading docks, or how I could build a whole new shelving system out in my garage. I'd just get up and start drawing out plans at the kitchen table while my wife was still asleep. 

And I felt... I felt fantastic. Like, unusually good. Fired up, you know? Like everything was finally clicking and I was the smartest guy in the room. I'd be walking the floor at work, talking a mile a minute to the guys, telling them how we were gonna break all the company records this quarter. I just felt this huge surge of energy, like I was plugged straight into a wall socket. 

But... there was another side to it, too. As good as I felt, I was also just... well, my wife called it being on a hair-trigger. If somebody didn't understand what I was saying right away, or if one of the forklift drivers was moving too slow, I wouldn't just correct them like I normally do. I'd snap. I mean, I'd really let them have it over the smallest things. Things I usually just let slide off my back. One time, my supervisor—the one who told me to come here—he asked me to double-check some inventory numbers, just standard protocol, and I practically bit his head off. I told him he was slowing me down and that I had it all figured out already. I felt so irritable, like everyone around me was just moving through molasses and getting in my way. It was like I was either on top of the world or ready to chew somebody out, and there was no in-between. And it lasted like that for weeks, right up until the bottom just completely fell out and I ended up where I am now.

Have there ever been times when your mood was extremely elevated or irritable, and you had so much energy that you didn’t need much sleep at all — and this was different enough that other people noticed or it caused problems?

Well, yeah, like I was just saying with the sleep and snapping at the guys at work... the energy I had, it was just unbelievable. I had so much energy for a while there that I didn't even know what to do with it all. I mean, I'd be up way before daylight. The house is pitch black, my wife is sound asleep, the streetlights are still on outside, and I'm already wide awake, buzzing like a fluorescent bulb. 

I'd be sitting there at the kitchen table in the dark, planning out all these warehouse changes. I was drawing up these big, elaborate maps on scrap paper, trying to figure out how to reroute the pallet jacks around the loading bays so we could shave, I don't know, maybe twenty seconds off every truck load. It made perfect sense to me at the time. But the thing is, I couldn't even just sit there and focus on that one thing. I'd be jumping from one job to the next without even wanting to stop. 

I'd get halfway through a drawing, then suddenly I'd be out in the garage, flipping the lights on and just going to town cleaning the whole place out. And I don't mean just sweeping the floor, I mean a full-blown, tear-it-down clean. I'd be pulling every single thing off the metal shelves, organizing all my wrenches by size, wiping down oil spots on the concrete, dragging out boxes of old junk we haven't looked at in ten years just to inventory what was in them. Then I'd leave that half-finished, march right back inside to work on the warehouse plans, and then maybe decide the hinges on the back door needed taking apart and oiling right that very second. 

I was just bouncing around like a pinball. My wife would come out to the kitchen for her coffee at 5:30 in the morning and just stare at me, because I had already done a full day's work before the sun even thought about coming up. I just couldn't stop moving, didn't *want* to stop moving. It felt like if I sat still for five minutes, I was wasting time. So, yeah, people definitely noticed, because you can't really hide it when you're tearing through the house and the warehouse like a tornado.
